summary: A schedule from BBN for adding more core memory to every IMP and TIP, the network's packet-switching machines, during early 1973. It lists the planned memory sizes after the upgrade and warns that TIPs would need more floor space. It was replaced by RFC 447.

eli5.summary: The people running the network's message-passing boxes announced when each box would be shut down for a memory upgrade, so everyone could plan around it.

subtitle: Schedule for upgrading the network's memory-bearing machines during early 1973.

tldr.problem: The packet-switching machines in ARPANET (IMPs and TIPs) needed more memory to handle growing network traffic, but the upgrades required shutting each machine down.
tldr.mechanism: BBN published a month-by-month schedule for retrofitting memory in each machine during early 1973, timed to coincide with each site's existing monthly preventive maintenance window.
tldr.outcome: The upgrades doubled memory in IMPs to 16K words and increased TIP memory from 16K to 28K or 32K words, but some TIPs had to expand to two cabinets.

today: RFC 434 is a historic maintenance schedule. It was superseded by RFC 447.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: During the first several months of 1973, BBN retrofitted every IMP (Interface Message Processor) and TIP (Terminal Interface Processor)—the network's packet-switching machines—with additional core memory. IMPs would receive 16K-word cores, and TIPs would be upgraded to 28K or 32K words depending on whether they had magnetic tape options.
sections.eli5: All the network's message routers were getting more memory to work faster.

sections.title: Impact on the Network
sections.content: The expansion of TIP core memory required some machines to grow to two cabinets, which meant sites needed to prepare additional floor space. The upgrades were scheduled during each site's normal monthly preventive maintenance window, but the work sometimes required longer downtime than a routine maintenance visit.
sections.eli5: Some computer boxes got bigger, so the computer rooms had to rearrange their space.

sections.title: Retrofit Schedule
sections.content: The schedule ran from January through April 1973, with sites distributed across all four months. Xerox and SAAC went in January, MIT and others in February and March, with the final machines such as Illinois scheduled for April. Sites that anticipated floor space problems were asked to contact BBN's Hawley Rising in advance.
sections.eli5: Each network location got an appointment for the upgrade, staggered so BBN could do them one at a time.
